## 402. What a line under a class must hold, and what a regularity takes in (PF)

PW's path to the future (07 §4.6) rested on steps 3 and 4 shown only in witnesses. Its owner asked that they be finished and that the open question be worked as philosophy ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-24-why-this-theory.md)). PF states both steps for every carrier, relation and class in a new core module, answers the finitude objection the philosophers' dossier raised against P2, and gives a first round of philosophical work ([study](../../development/pf-path-and-crux/PHILOSOPHY-ROUND-1.md)). An independent review of the first build (a separate Claude Opus agent, read-only) made twelve findings, all taken, as listed there.

```text
Result(s): new record what-a-line-holds-and-a-regularity-takes-in.

       everything downstream of anything alike to a member whose effects the class holds («所缘同于») is alike to it
```

**What it says.** Given a regularity, the wide scope of §4.6 is equivalent to its first step: everything downstream of one's acts lies on one's line exactly where everything one conditions does. The regularity does real work, and the reach rests on one premise beside it, holding one's effects. Finitude does not break P2's distinction: constancy up to the net's end tells a family's class from the organism's in a finite net, where constancy itself picks out nothing.

**Constructivity.** No omniscience principle; the decided region in «所经必同» is what lets the proof ask whether an occurrence is still inside. The receipt's empty axiom report is the evidence.
